[project]
name = "torchannex"
version = "0.0.0"
description = "Curated distribution of PyTorch-compatible Python sub-libraries (the PyTorch annex)"
readme = "README.md"
license = "BSD-3-Clause"
authors = [{ name = "PyTorch Team", email = "packages@pytorch.org" }]
keywords = ["pytorch", "torch", "metapackage", "distribution"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 1 - Planning",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Artificial Intelligence",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]

# This is the initial PyPI namespace-reservation release. It intentionally has
# no dependencies. Real releases will be versioned in lockstep with PyTorch
# (see README.md) and will pin `torch ~= X.Y.0` plus the curated annex packages.
dependencies = []

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/pytorch/annex"
Issues = "https://github.com/pytorch/annex/issues"

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=77"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

# torchannex ships no Python source; it is a pure metapackage whose only job
# is to express a set of pinned dependencies. The empty lists below tell
# setuptools there are no modules or packages to find.
[tool.setuptools]
py-modules = []
packages = []

# torchannex

`torchannex` is a curated distribution ("annex") of small, pure-Python
libraries that extend PyTorch. Installing `torchannex` gives you a set of
sub-libraries pinned to versions that are known to be compatible with a
specific PyTorch release, although these libraries are intended to be loosely
coupled with PyTorch and therefore compatible with a variety of releases.

The annex is designed to be *cheap*: every package in it is a lightweight pure
Python package that installs instantly and pulls in no heavy native
dependencies of its own beyond PyTorch.

## When should I use `torchannex`?

You do **not** have to depend on `torchannex` directly. Two patterns are
supported:

1. **Batteries-included.** Depend on `torchannex`. You get the full curated
   set, versioned in lockstep with the PyTorch release you have installed.
2. **Hand-picked.** Depend on the individual annex packages you care about and
   pin them yourself. Useful when you have an opinion about a specific
   sub-library's version and do not want the whole set.

The annex packages are ordinary PyPI packages. The metapackage is a
convenience, not a gate.

## Installation

```bash
pip install torchannex
# or
uv pip install torchannex
```

If `torch` is already installed (or pinned elsewhere in your environment),
the resolver will select the `torchannex` version whose PyTorch pin matches:

```bash
pip install "torch==2.5.3" torchannex   # resolves to torchannex 2.5.x
```

## Versioning

`torchannex` versions track PyTorch on the `X.Y` components only:

| Component | Meaning                                                         |
|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `X`       | PyTorch major version (lockstep)                                |
| `Y`       | PyTorch minor version (lockstep)                                |
| `Z`       | Independent annex bugfix counter for the `X.Y` series            |

A `torchannex X.Y.Z` release depends on `torch ~= X.Y.0` (i.e.
`>= X.Y.0, < X.(Y+1).0`). This means:

- Any `torch X.Y.*` patch release is compatible with any `torchannex X.Y.*`.
- If we ship a fix to an annex sub-library without a new PyTorch release, we
  bump only the annex `Z`. For example, for the PyTorch 2.5 series:
  - `torchannex 2.5.0` — first annex release for torch 2.5
  - `torchannex 2.5.1` — bugfix to an annex sub-library (torch unchanged)
  - `torchannex 2.5.2` — another annex bugfix
- When PyTorch 2.6 ships we start a new series at `torchannex 2.6.0`.

### Relationship between `torch` Z and `torchannex` Z

They are **independent**. `torchannex 2.5.7` does **not** imply `torch 2.5.7`;
it simply means the 8th annex release cut for the 2.5 series. Whatever `torch
2.5.*` you have installed is fine.

## What's in the annex?

In the short term, we plan to put `spmd_types` in the annex to allow for some
closer integration with DTensor local map.

## Building and releasing

`torchannex` is a pure metapackage — no Python source — built with
setuptools. The empty `py-modules` / `packages` entries in `pyproject.toml`
tell setuptools there is nothing to find.

```bash
uv build       # produces sdist and wheel
uv publish     # uploads to PyPI (requires credentials)
```

See `TESTING.md` for the manual acceptance tests to run before a release.

## License

BSD-3-Clause.

# Manual testing plan for `torchannex`

`torchannex` is a metapackage whose correctness is entirely determined by
whether the PyPA-standard dependency resolvers (pip, uv) pick the right
version in practice. This document is the manual acceptance test that should
be run before every release.

The tests below fall into three phases:

1. **Pre-`0.0.0`** — sanity checks before uploading anything.
2. **Post-`0.0.0`** — sanity checks after the namespace-reservation upload.
3. **Post-real-release** — end-to-end resolver checks once real `X.Y.Z`
   releases exist.

For the post-release phases, use **TestPyPI** first (`--index-url
https://test.pypi.org/simple/ --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple/`)
before cutting a real PyPI release. That lets us exercise resolver behavior
without polluting PyPI.

Throughout, always use a **fresh virtualenv** per test so there is no state
from a previous run. A convenient harness:

```bash
mktest () {
    python3.12 -m venv /tmp/tatest && /tmp/tatest/bin/pip install -U pip uv
    export PATH=/tmp/tatest/bin:$PATH
}
rmtest () { rm -rf /tmp/tatest; }
```

---

## Phase 1: Pre-`0.0.0` local build

Verify the wheel builds as a true metapackage (no Python source) and installs
cleanly.

```bash
uv build
unzip -l dist/torchannex-0.0.0-*.whl
```

**Expected:** the wheel contains only `.dist-info/` entries — no `.py` files,
no `torchannex/` directory.

```bash
pip install dist/torchannex-0.0.0-*.whl
python -c "import importlib.metadata as m; print(m.version('torchannex'))"
# 0.0.0
python -c "import torchannex"
# ModuleNotFoundError — expected, this is a metapackage
```

**Pass criteria:** version reports `0.0.0`; importing `torchannex` errors
(metapackage has no module).

---

## Phase 2: Post-`0.0.0` reservation

After uploading `0.0.0` to PyPI, verify that fresh resolvers see it.

### T2.1 — plain install picks 0.0.0

```bash
pip install torchannex
pip show torchannex  # Version: 0.0.0
```

```bash
uv pip install torchannex
uv pip show torchannex  # Version: 0.0.0
```

**Pass criteria:** both resolvers install `0.0.0` with no other packages
pulled in.

### T2.2 — reservation does not conflict with arbitrary torch

```bash
pip install "torch" torchannex
```

**Pass criteria:** `torch` installs at its latest version alongside
`torchannex==0.0.0`. The empty-deps `0.0.0` does not constrain `torch`.

---

## Phase 3: Post-real-release resolver tests

These tests assume at least one real release exists, e.g. `torchannex
2.5.0` pinning `torch ~= 2.5.0` and at least one annex sub-library. Ideally,
run them after a release that has two bugfix variants (`2.5.0` and `2.5.1`)
so the "prefer highest `Z`" behavior can be verified.

### T3.1 — no constraints, latest torchannex wins

```bash
pip install torchannex
pip show torchannex                 # highest X.Y.Z
pip show torch                      # matching X.Y.*
```

```bash
uv pip install torchannex
```

**Pass criteria:** resolver picks the newest `torchannex` and the newest
compatible `torch`. The `0.0.0` placeholder is *never* preferred over a real
release because version ordering puts it lowest.

### T3.2 — torch pin drives torchannex selection (backtracking)

Pre-pinning the PyTorch minor series should force the resolver to backtrack
into the matching `torchannex X.Y.*` line.

Suppose releases `2.5.1`, `2.6.0` exist on PyPI:

```bash
pip install "torch==2.5.3" torchannex
pip show torchannex                 # 2.5.1  (highest Z in 2.5 series)
pip show torch                      # 2.5.3  (honored)
```

```bash
uv pip install "torch==2.5.3" torchannex
```

**Pass criteria:** both resolvers pick `torchannex 2.5.1`, not `2.6.0`.
`torch` stays at the pinned `2.5.3`.

> **Why this works.** `torchannex 2.6.0` declares `torch ~= 2.6.0` which is
> incompatible with `torch==2.5.3`. The resolver backtracks to the next
> candidate, `torchannex 2.5.1`, whose `torch ~= 2.5.0` accepts `2.5.3`.

### T3.3 — torch already installed, then torchannex

```bash
pip install "torch==2.5.3"
pip install torchannex                           # second invocation
pip show torchannex                              # should be 2.5.x, not 2.6.x
```

**Pass criteria:** the second `pip install` does not attempt to upgrade
`torch` to 2.6 just to satisfy the latest `torchannex`. It picks the
compatible 2.5 line. (This is pip's default "only-if-needed" upgrade
strategy; be explicit if we test `--upgrade-strategy eager` behavior.)

Repeat with `uv pip` and confirm the same outcome.

### T3.4 — `--upgrade` upgrades both together

```bash
pip install "torch==2.5.0" torchannex            # seed env
pip install --upgrade torch torchannex
pip show torch                                    # bumped to latest 2.Y.*
pip show torchannex                               # bumped to latest Y series
```

**Pass criteria:** both packages move together. If the latest `torch` is
`2.6.0`, `torchannex` should be the latest `2.6.*`.

### T3.5 — unsatisfiable combination errors cleanly

```bash
pip install "torch==2.4.0" torchannex
```

**Pass criteria:** resolver fails (no `torchannex` exists that accepts
`torch 2.4`). The error message clearly names the conflict rather than
silently installing a wrong version.

Repeat with `uv pip install "torch==2.4.0" torchannex` — expect a similar
clean conflict report.

### T3.6 — hand-picked sub-libraries, no torchannex

```bash
pip install some-annex-subpkg
```

**Pass criteria:** the individual annex package installs and pulls in an
appropriate `torch`, exactly as if the metapackage did not exist. Users who
skip `torchannex` should hit no friction.

### T3.7 — bugfix pickup within the same torch series

Pre-condition: `torchannex 2.5.0` and `torchannex 2.5.1` both exist.

```bash
pip install "torch==2.5.3" "torchannex==2.5.0"   # seed with older annex
pip install --upgrade torchannex                 # upgrade within series
pip show torchannex                              # 2.5.1
pip show torch                                   # still 2.5.3
```

**Pass criteria:** the upgrade picks up the annex bugfix without touching
`torch`.

### T3.8 — `uv add` in a project

```bash
uv init --bare /tmp/consumer && cd /tmp/consumer
uv add torch==2.5.3 torchannex
cat pyproject.toml
```

**Pass criteria:** the written-out constraint for `torchannex` resolves to
the `2.5.*` line in `uv.lock`.

---

## Regression checklist

When cutting a new `torchannex X.Y.Z`:

- [ ] Phase 1 build test passes (wheel is source-less).
- [ ] T3.1 picks the new release.
- [ ] T3.2 still works for each still-supported `X.Y` series we ship
      (i.e. if we also maintain `torchannex 2.5.*`, pinning `torch==2.5.3`
      still resolves there after a 2.6 release).
- [ ] T3.5 still produces a clean error for out-of-range torch pins.
- [ ] `pip install torchannex==X.Y.Z` on the oldest and newest Python
      versions that `torch X.Y.*` supports. (`torchannex` itself sets no
      `requires-python`; the floor comes transitively from `torch` and the
      annex sub-libraries.)

---

## Notes on resolver internals

- Both pip (resolvelib) and uv (PubGrub) backtrack on version conflicts, so
  the "torch pin drives torchannex selection" property holds for both.
- Versions containing only numeric components (no `a`/`b`/`rc`/`dev`) are
  compared by PEP 440 ordering; `2.6.0 > 2.5.1 > 2.5.0 > 0.0.0`. This is the
  basis for why `0.0.0` is never selected once real releases exist.
- If we ever need to fully retract `0.0.0`, use PyPI's **yank** feature —
  do not delete — so lockfiles that happen to reference it keep working.
